questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Small city and student city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were only student living in the town and so many different societies and clubs which is perfect if you are travelling alone or like the social life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university sends personal emails all the time helping you in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was in contact with a person from the university on my arrival day that helped me with everything. After receiving my key they drove me to the accommodation. Everything was very good and easy.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many options at different prices - Pictures, prices, descriptions and budgets can be found on the university website.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were shops 5-15 minutes walking. We were 10 people sharing a big kitchen with plenty of space.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You need to buy all kitchen stuff yourselves. There is a kitchen package though the university but its cheaper to buy the essentials in town.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only lived with international students which was great. The accommodation was fine for one or two semester but most people move to town after the first semester.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was easy and if there was any problems with courses or registration there was plenty of help.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was 3-4 documents to complete. The big problems could be the availability of the courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was plenty of help from the host university with very quick responds time

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my three courses in the first attempt for applying. My friend had to register for another class after which prolonged her registering for 3-4 weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for help, use the other students going and attend to the zoom meetings.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It depends on your English level. The lectures was a bit tricky but everything was recorded. In general the level was easier but it also depends on the courses you are taking.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lectures and practice classes was very similar to KU. There was 2-3 assignments though the semester in each course which was a part of the grade. That reduced some of the exams pressure. The exams only weighted 40-50% of the grade. I had 9 days to finish two of my exams and 24 hours for the last one (because of corona).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to programming 
Behavioural Neurobiology 
Evolution and Molecular Systematics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was very happy with the computer science department - They had free help sessions every day for two hours. Biology department was also good. It depends on what you like but overall was science very good - A was a bit difficult to combine programming and biology.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Kitchen stuff and the many trips we went on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: There were more trips and fun stuff which was more expensive than the budget - It was worth it though

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were over 50 different societies and clubs. The sport center with swimming pool was free for all students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was in the hiking club and aber ski for social events. There is something for everybody. There was events almost every day which was a lot of fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit all the countries in UK by train. We went to Dublin, Cardiff, Manchester, Birmingham and Scotland for Christmas. Plenty of opportunities for things to do in the weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
I lived with people from 5 different countries which could be challenging at times but very educational. I've learned a lot by living with different people and had a lot of fun. 

The English culture was easy to adjust

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be nice and social. Go to the social event in the beginning

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not any cultural differences that was challenging. The student was very young compared to when Danish student begin their studies.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language and the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: small but a student town, many social events and very good university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a perfect town for 1-2 semester with a lot of social events and nice people. Many international students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people a met and the friendships. I've leaned so much about myself and can today see a big change. It was some of the best decisions I've ever made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to classes alone and ask for help without thinking about what people think.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Aber is an amazing student town. It is small but there is a lot to do in the town and plenty of opportunities to travel in UK. It is a lot like collage with many societies, living on campus and many parties.  student facilities.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
